name: EFM32G230F128G-E-QFN64
title: EFM32 Gecko: 32-bit ARM Cortex-M3 microcontrollers, 32 MHz, up to 128 kB flash and 16 kB RAM, AES, 12-bit ADC and DAC, QFN32 to BGA112
summary: A family of low-power 32-bit microcontrollers on the ARM Cortex-M3 core at up to 32 MHz, with 16 to 128 kB of flash and 8 or 16 kB of RAM, running from 1.98 V to 3.8 V. They draw 180 µA/MHz running from flash, 0.9 µA in Deep Sleep with the RTC on, 0.6 µA in Stop and 20 nA in Shutoff, and wake in 2 µs. Peripherals include up to three USARTs, two low-energy UARTs, I2C, three 16-bit timers, a low-energy timer, an RTC, three pulse counters, an 8-channel DMA, hardware AES, a 12-bit 1 Msps ADC, a 12-bit DAC and two analog comparators, with an LCD controller and an external bus on some members. EFM32G230F128G-E-QFN64 is the QFN64 part with 128 kB of flash, 16 kB of RAM and 56 GPIO.
key_figures: 128 kB / 16 kB (EFM32G230F128G); family 16 to 128 kB / 8 or 16 kB
180 µA/MHz at 3 V (EM0, code from flash)
45 µA/MHz EM1; 0.9 µA EM2; 0.6 µA EM3; 20 nA EM4 (3 V)
12-bit, 1 Msps, 8 external inputs on the G230
3 × USART, 2 × LEUART, I2C, 3 × 16-bit TIMER, LETIMER, 24-bit RTC, 3 × PCNT, 2 × ACMP, VCMP, AES, 8-ch DMA, 8-ch PRS
QFN32, TQFP48, QFN64, TQFP64, LQFP100, BGA112 (G230: QFN64)

operation.text: Up to 90 GPIO pins with push-pull, open-drain, pull-up or pull-down, input filter and drive strength settings, peripheral signals routable to several pin locations, 16 asynchronous external interrupts, and output states held through Shutoff with wake-up from it. An 8-channel DMA controller and an 8-channel Peripheral Reflex System. Three 16-bit timers with three compare/capture/PWM channels each (dead-time insertion on TIMER0), a 16-bit low-energy timer, a 24-bit real-time counter, three 8-bit pulse counters and a watchdog on its own 50 nA RC oscillator. Up to three USARTs (UART, SPI, ISO 7816 smart card, IrDA, I2S; triple buffered, full or half duplex), one UART, two low-energy UARTs and an I2C with SMBus support. A 12-bit 1 Msps ADC with 8 single-ended or 4 differential inputs and a temperature sensor, a 12-bit 500 ksps DAC with 2 single-ended or 1 differential output, two analog comparators with capacitive sensing on up to 16 inputs, and a supply voltage comparator. An LCD controller for up to 4×40 segments and an external bus interface for up to 4×64 MB on the members that have them. A brown-out detector and power-on reset, Serial Wire debug on 2 pins with a 1-pin Serial Wire viewer, and a factory-loaded UART bootloader.

Five modes, run by the Energy Management Unit, which also cuts power to unused SRAM blocks. EM0 Run: 180 µA/MHz at 3 V executing from flash. EM1 Sleep: 45 µA/MHz at 3 V. EM2 Deep Sleep: 0.9 µA at 3 V with the RTC and its 32.768 kHz oscillator running; RAM, CPU state, brown-out detection and power-on reset all retained. EM3 Stop: 0.6 µA at 3 V, again keeping RAM, CPU state, brown-out detection and power-on reset. EM4 Shutoff: 20 nA at 3 V. Wake-up takes 2 µs. Lowest mode in which each block still works: LETIMER, RTC, LEUART (with DMA) and LCD in EM2; I2C address recognition and the pulse counter in EM3; GPIO wake-up and pin state retention in EM4.

The EFM32 Gecko (G) family shares one Cortex-M3 core and differs by package and peripheral set. G200 and G210 are QFN32 (24 GPIO; the G200 has no AES), G222 is TQFP48 (37 GPIO), G230 and G840 are QFN64 (56 GPIO), G232 and G842 are TQFP64 (53 GPIO), G280 and G880 are LQFP100 (86 GPIO), and G290 and G890 are BGA112 (90 GPIO). The 8xx members add the LCD controller; G280, G290, G880 and G890 add the external bus interface and UART0. Flash is 16, 32, 64 or 128 kB, with 8 kB of RAM on the 16 and 32 kB parts and 16 kB on the 64 and 128 kB parts. Every member runs up to 32 MHz from 1.98 V to 3.8 V over -40 to 85 °C. EFM32G230F128G-E-QFN64 is the QFN64 member with 128 kB of flash and 16 kB of RAM, no LCD and no EBI.

Reading an ordering code such as EFM32G890F128G-E-BGA112R from the left: EFM32 (energy friendly 32-bit microcontroller), G (Gecko), a feature-set code (890), F (flash memory), the flash size in kB (128), the temperature grade G (-40 to +85 °C), the revision (E), the package (BGA) and its pin count (112). A trailing R orders tape and reel.

ARM Cortex-M3, a 32-bit RISC processor at up to 32 MHz giving up to 1.25 Dhrystone MIPS/MHz, with a memory protection unit of up to 8 segments, a wake-up interrupt controller that takes interrupts while the CPU sleeps, and a SysTick timer.

Serial Wire debug on two pins (DBG_SWCLK, DBG_SWDIO), plus a Serial Wire viewer output (DBG_SWO) that carries profiling, data trace and software messages. SWCLK (internal pull-down) and SWDIO (internal pull-up) are on their pins from reset; SWO stays off until software turns it on.

The Memory System Controller runs the flash, which both the CPU and the DMA can read and write. The flash has a main block for program code and an information block holding user data and the lock bits, plus a read-only page of system and calibration data. Flash read and write work in EM0 and EM1. The family carries 128, 64, 32 or 16 kB of flash and 16 or 8 kB of RAM.

An ARM PL230 µDMA controller with 8 channels moves data without the CPU, for instance from a USART to RAM or from the EBI to a timer making PWM, so the part can stay in a low-energy mode while data moves.

The Reset Management Unit handles the part's resets. Power-on reset and the brown-out detector stay on down to EM3. RESETn is active low with an internal pull-up; an external reset source should only pull it low.

Oscillators: a high-frequency crystal oscillator, a high-frequency RC oscillator, an auxiliary high-frequency RC oscillator, a low-frequency crystal oscillator (32.768 kHz typ), a low-frequency RC oscillator, and the watchdog's own RC oscillator. The Clock Management Unit turns each oscillator on or off and configures it, and gates the clock of each peripheral on its own, so software need not spend power on peripherals and oscillators that are idle. HFXTAL_N and LFXTAL_N also accept an external clock. CMU_CLK0 and CMU_CLK1 bring clocks out to pins.
The watchdog resets the part when the system fails, whether from software or from an outside event such as an ESD pulse. It runs on a dedicated RC oscillator at 50 nA.

A network of 8 channels that carries signals from producer peripherals straight to consumer peripherals, which act on them without the CPU. Edge triggers and other handling can be applied along the way. A GPIO input can be routed through it to other peripherals.

On G280, G290, G880 and G890: a memory-mapped parallel bus for asynchronous devices such as SRAM, flash, ADCs and LCD modules, reached by software as ordinary memory accesses. Address and data share lines (EBI_AD[15:0]) to save pins, with EBI_ALE, EBI_WEn, EBI_REn, EBI_ARDY and four chip selects; timing is adjustable to the device. Four regions of 64 MB each sit at 0x80000000 to 0x8fffffff.

One I2C, master or slave, multi-master capable, at standard, fast and fast-mode plus speeds from 10 kbit/s to 1 Mbit/s. Slave arbitration and timeouts allow an SMBus system. Transfers can be run byte by byte or close to automatically. Slave address recognition works in every energy mode down to EM3.
Up to three USARTs (USART0, USART1, USART2): full-duplex asynchronous UART, RS-485, SPI, MicroWire and 3-wire, ISO 7816 smart cards and I2S, triple buffered. USART0 carries IrDA.
A UART bootloader (application note AN0003) is programmed at the factory, with autobaud and destructive write. It uses BOOT_TX and BOOT_RX, on PE10 and PE11.
UART0, on G280, G290, G880 and G890: asynchronous serial in full or half duplex.
Two low-energy UARTs work from a 32.768 kHz clock alone, up to 9600 baud, in both directions, and keep running in EM2 with the DMA, needing little software.

Three 16-bit timers (TIMER0 to TIMER2), each with three compare/capture channels for input capture, compare output and PWM. TIMER0 adds dead-time insertion with complementary outputs (TIM0_CDTI[2:0]) for motor control.
A 24-bit real-time counter clocked by the 32.768 kHz crystal oscillator or the 32.768 kHz RC oscillator. It runs in EM0, EM1 and EM2, so it keeps time while most of the part is off.
A 16-bit low-energy timer that runs in EM0, EM1 and EM2 and drives waveforms on its outputs with little software. It is linked to the RTC and can start counting on an RTC compare match.
Three 8-bit pulse counters (PCNT0 to PCNT2) count pulses on one input or decode quadrature signals. Each is clocked from LFACLK or from its PCNTn_S0IN pin, and works in EM0 to EM3.

Two comparators (ACMP0, ACMP1) each give a digital output telling which of two inputs is higher. Each input is a pin or an internal reference. The bias current sets the response time and current draw. Capacitive sensing works on up to 16 inputs.
The VCMP watches the supply voltage and can raise an interrupt when the supply crosses a programmable level in either direction. Its bias current sets the response time and current draw.

A successive-approximation ADC of up to 12 bits at up to 1 Msps. Its input multiplexer selects from 8 external pins and 6 internal signals, and the part has an on-chip temperature sensor; the pins can be used as 8 single-ended or 4 differential inputs. All eight inputs, ADC0_CH0 to ADC0_CH7, are on pins of the G230.

A 12-bit, 500 ksps, fully differential rail-to-rail DAC with two single-ended output buffers that can be joined into one differential output; suited to sensor interfaces and sound. Both outputs, DAC0_OUT0 and DAC0_OUT1, are on pins of the G230.

An AES accelerator that encrypts and decrypts using keys of 128 or 256 bits, on every member but the G200. One 128-bit block takes 52 HFCORECLK cycles with a 128-bit key (54 in the family's feature list) and 75 with a 256-bit key. It is an AHB slave for fast access to its data and key registers, and takes 32-bit writes only; 8-bit and 16-bit writes are not supported.

Pins are grouped in ports of up to 16 (A to F). Each pin is an input or output with open-drain, filter and drive strength set per pin. Peripherals such as timer PWM outputs or USARTs take over pins and can be routed to several locations. Up to 16 asynchronous external interrupts can come from any pin, and a pin's input can go through the PRS to other peripherals. The G230 has 56 GPIO.

On the 8xx members: drives a segment LCD of up to 4×40 segments. A voltage boost gives the panel more than the supply voltage, contrast is adjustable, and animation runs without the CPU. It keeps working in EM2 and its frame counter interrupt can wake the part at regular intervals to update the display. With the booster in use, a 22 nF capacitor joins LCD_BCAP_P and LCD_BCAP_N, and 1 uF goes from LCD_BEXT to VSS; with the booster off, LCD_BEXT may take an external LCD voltage, or be left open or used as GPIO when AVDD powers the LCD directly.

Typical figures are at TAMB = 25 °C and VDD = 3.0 V unless a row says otherwise. Minimum and maximum figures cover the worst case of ambient temperature, supply voltage and frequency inside the general operating conditions unless a row says otherwise.
These are stress limits only: the part is not guaranteed to work at them, and going past them can damage it or shorten its life. Normal operation is bounded by the general operating conditions.
Wake-up from EM1 takes no HFCORECLK cycles, from EM2 and EM3 about 2 µs and from EM4 about 163 µs, each counted from the trigger to the CPU's first clock edge.

AVDD_x, VDD_DREG and IOVDD_x are joined on the board, with a filter between them where one is wanted; AN0002 (EFM32 Hardware Design Considerations) gives schematic guidance. The regulator output on DECOUPLE takes a 1 µF capacitor to ground, X5R recommended. After a power-on, brown-out or pin reset, code starts running about 163 µs after reset is released; a reset pulse on the pin is at least 50 ns.

Input low is guaranteed up to 0.30×VDD and input high from 0.70×VDD, with at least 0.1×VDD of hysteresis over 1.98 V to 3.8 V; an input sitting between 0.3×VDD and 0.7×VDD raises the supply current. Pull-up and pull-down resistors are 40 kΩ typical, and the glitch filter removes pulses of 10 ns to 50 ns.

The LFXO runs a 32.768 kHz crystal of up to 120 kΩ ESR with up to 25 pF load. The Configurator in Simplicity Studio gives the load capacitance and software settings for safe start-up of a given crystal; AN0016 (EFM32 Oscillator Design Consideration) covers crystal configuration.

The TUNING field of CMU_HFRCOCTRL moves the HFRCO by about 0.3 % per LSB, and the bands above 7 MHz overlap across supply and temperature, so firmware calibrating against the LFXO or HFXO can hold any frequency from 7 MHz to 28 MHz. The AUXHFRCO is trimmed the same way through CMU_AUXHFRCOCTRL, about 0.3 % per LSB, within its 14 MHz band.

The ACMP's total current is its own active current plus that of its internal reference, which is zero when an external reference is used. Likewise the LCD's total current is its steady-state current plus the boost converter's share, zero with the boost off.
PCB design guidance for the EFM32G is in application note AN0002, EFM32 Hardware Design Considerations.

In the pin tables, a peripheral signal's possible locations are written '#n', several on one pin joined by '/'. The location is chosen in the LOCATION field of the module's *_ROUTE register. Signals with no alternative, such as analog inputs, appear under LOCATION 0. Board design guidance is in application note AN0002.

The top carries a dot orientation mark and four lines: the family name EFM32; the chip version (for example G890F128) followed by a temperature-grade letter (G) and a revision letter (B); a production code; and the core name Cortex-M3.

The TQFP48, QFN64 and QFN32 packages are built on a nickel-palladium-gold preplated leadframe. Every EFM32 package is RoHS compliant and contains no bromine (Br) or antimony (Sb).

Each carries a dot orientation mark and four lines: EFM32; the chip version (for example TG110F8) followed by a temperature-grade letter (G); the first part of the production code (C1C197); and the rest of the production code (1015) followed by the revision letter (B).
The silicon revision is the revision letter in the package marking.
Lead-free reflow follows the current IPC/JEDEC J-STD-020 recommendations.
